Jot guides

  • Writing in Jot: how to write a .jot journal by hand: dates, tasks, notes, ratings. Ten minutes; the first section is enough to start.
  • Using the template editor: design a journal's shape and download it as a .jot file to fill in, on a computer, a phone or InkDeck. Its Numbers and charts section covers the weekly dashboard: numbers each day, a chart of the week.
  • Automation and connections: put your events on your calendar, bring in numbers from a fitness app, carry tasks forward, and connect to other services (webhooks, Todoist, the weather), only when you ask.
  • Converting an old diary: turn a diary kept as plain text (your own, or one from Project Gutenberg) into dated Jot entries.
  • Turning anything into Jot: chats, notes, meeting minutes, spreadsheets and photographed pages, with an AI agent's help (the to-jot skill), and jot check to see that a file is valid.

To see Jot at length, the Examples page has whole public-domain diaries converted to .jot.

These guides are also pages on the site (/guide/), built from these files by site/build-guides.mjs. The full rules are in the Jot specification.
